transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-05-09
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 12 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Cho (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood PM), Lena Ortiz (BlueOak Head of ML), Marcus Hale (BlueOak Infra), Priya Singh (BlueOak PM)
Shared links: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/optimize-sandbox, sandbox: https://redwood.app/sandbox/blueoak, perf sheet: https://sheets.redwood/blueoak-q-sweep

SUMMARY:
Quick Optimize console walkthrough focused on fallback sensitivity (how conservative our rollbacks are when fidelity drops), telemetry retention and debug traces, and running an INT8 vs FP8 sweep in the customer sandbox. Lena wants low-latency interactive queries for clinicians (p95 target <= 200ms) but tolerates occasional quality drops for bulk inference. Discussed rollback thresholds, canary windows, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed to spin up a sandbox and run a sensitivity sweep with BlueOak prompts.

TOPICS COVERED:
- Console: precision profiles and fallback policy editor
- Telemetry: per-call traces, tokens breakdown, prefix cache hits
- Quantization sweep: INT8 vs FP8, mixed precision fallback
- Rollback thresholds and canary window sizing
- Security & compliance notes (VPC, KMS, SOC2)

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna do a quick Optimize console walkthrough focusing on fallback sensitivity and the telemetry you get in the sandbox. Evan will drive the demo. Uh Samir's here for product questions.
[00:18] Evan Cho: Hi all. I pulled the BlueOak sandbox config so you can see a live run. Quick note: some of the names in the console are abbreviated, and the auto-transcribe sometimes shows "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" so heads up.
[00:33] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Our main ask is interactive latency for clinician workflows, target p95 at or under 200ms, but we also want to test INT8 because cost is a concern. We can tolerate occasional hallucination for non-critical queries.
[00:46] Marcus Hale: Also need to validate audit logs and KMS integration before we can move to Dedicated. SOC two reports are required for our compliance team.
[00:56] Maya Patel: Yep, we'll share SOC2 and our KMS integration guide. For the demo: first show fallback policy editor, then show a quant sweep report comparing INT8 and FP8 with quality metrics.
[01:12] Evan Cho: Opening the Optimize console... (click) here's the precision profiles page. You can see a "fidelity lane" for the clinician model. The UI shows expected latency delta and cost per million tokens for each profile. You can set fallback rules like "if ROUGE drops > 3% over canary, revert to higher-precision model". Note: auto transcribed as "rouge" but we talked about "qscore" metric mapped to your evals.
[01:40] Priya Singh: How often does the canary evaluate? We need quick rollback for user-facing flows.
[01:47] Evan Cho: Default canary window is 1 hour with 5k requests, but you can do time or request-count windows and a sliding threshold. For interactive paths I recommend a 10-15 minute canary with tighter thresholds.
[02:05] Lena Ortiz: What about telemetry? We need traces to show where latency spikes are happening — is there token-level timing?
[02:12] Evan Cho: Yes, you get per-call traces with token timing and a breakdown (model compute, queue time, KV cache hit). Console can surface tail latency percentiles and trace samples. In sandbox we keep 14 days by default but for pilots we can extend to 30 days (note: could be extra cost).
[02:35] Marcus Hale: And logs for every inference? We need to be sure PII isn't stored — do you support redaction or never-log mode?
[02:42] Maya Patel: Redwood supports configurable retention and redaction rules, plus VPC/private deployment options. We'll send the redaction policy doc.

[03:05] Evan Cho: Switching to the quant sweep. I ran an INT8 vs FP8 sweep on your prompt set overnight. Live sheet linked in chat. Here's the heatmap: FP8 shows smaller quality delta for long-form summaries but higher variance at tail, INT8 reduces cost by ~38% with small median latency improvements but p99 shows occasional spikes due to fallback triggers.
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: Can you explain the fallback spike cause?
[03:38] Evan Cho: Sure — when the model hits a failure case or low confidence on some tokens, our runtime will route that request to a higher-precision variant if the fallback policy is set to immediate. That adds extra latency for those requests; with canaries you can tune how sensitive that route is.
[03:55] Samir Gupta: Also worth noting that mixed-precision modes can do per-layer fallback instead of whole-request fallback, which reduces latency variance but is slightly more complex to roll out.
[04:10] Priya Singh: How do we control cost vs fidelity centrally? We want a global budget and per-route overrides.
[04:17] Evan Cho: Optimize supports cost budget rules. You can set global budgets with per-route caps and priority lanes — e.g., clinician interactive lane pinned to FP8 with higher cost allowance, background batch lane pinned to INT8.

[04:38] Maya Patel: Quick demo of editing a fallback rule: (typing) here's the rule for "summarize-clinical-note" route: currently will fall back from INT8 to FP8 if fidelity metric drops >2% within 15 min canary. I'll change sensitivity to 3% and widen canary to 30 minutes to reduce flapping.
[05:03] Evan Cho: Watch the estimated impact: the console recalculates estimated cost and expected rollback rate instantly based on past traffic.
[05:17] Marcus Hale: Are those estimates based on our actual traces or a model-level baseline?
[05:22] Evan Cho: They use your sandbox traces plus model performance profiles in the catalog. If you have insufficient data, it will show conservative defaults.

[05:35] Lena Ortiz: About quality metrics — can we plug in our in-house evals? We compute a clinical correctness score.
[05:41] Samir Gupta: Yes, you can upload custom evals and map them to a fidelity metric. Console supports custom metrics; they show up in the canary dashboard.
[05:52] Priya Singh: Any gotchas with FP8? We've heard about stability issues on some workloads.
[05:57] Evan Cho: FP8 tends to be more stable on long-context retrieval tasks but may underperform on low-data prompts. In the sweep we flagged 2 prompt templates with regression; we'll share the sample IDs. Also sometimes the transcription wrote "eff p eight" in the notes.

[06:18] Evan Cho: I'm going to trigger a simulated failure in INT8 to show rollback. (simulates) You can see the request routed to the FP8 variant; trace shows extra 120ms latency on that sample. Console highlights the rollback event and attaches the trace.
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: That's useful. Can we get alerts on rollback rate crossing a threshold?
[06:43] Evan Cho: Absolutely — you can set alerts (Slack/email) for rollback rate, fidelity delta, or cost burn rate.

[07:00] Maya Patel: Questions about security/compliance?
[07:05] Marcus Hale: KMS integration — we need HSM-backed keys. Do you support customer-managed keys in a Dedicated/private deployment?
[07:12] Maya Patel: Yes, both VPC private control plane and on-prem options support CMKs and HSMs. We'll include the deployment matrix in the email.
[07:22] Lena Ortiz: How does data residency work? We need EU region for some datasets.
[07:27] Maya Patel: You can pin to regionally hosted endpoints; private deployments give you full control.

[07:38] Evan Cho: Back to telemetry — we also surface a "sensitivity curve" visual: x-axis is sensitivity threshold (percent fidelity drop), y-axis is expected rollback rate. This helps pick a conservative working point.
[07:50] Priya Singh: Can we run an automated sweep across sensitivity values and get a decision matrix?
[07:56] Evan Cho: Yes, the console has a "sensitivity sweep" job that runs your prompt set across specified thresholds and outputs a matrix with cost, expected rollback %, and quality deltas for each route.
[08:09] Samir Gupta: For pilots we typically run three sweeps: baseline, aggressive (low threshold) and conservative (high threshold) and then pick a middle ground.

[08:24] Lena Ortiz: What does rollout look like operationally? We have a small ML infra team.
[08:29] Evan Cho: Typical sequence: sandbox sweep -> small canary (10% traffic) for 24h -> expand to 50% -> full. You can do A/B comparisons in the console and tie rollouts to impressions and user impact.
[08:43] Marcus Hale: Who owns the rollback when it's automated? We need clear audit trail.
[08:49] Maya Patel: The audit log shows who edited policies and automatic rollback events with trace IDs; you can set whether to auto-rollback or only alert.

[09:05] Priya Singh: Let's talk about pricing signals — if we set a global budget, do you throttle or fallback to cheaper models automatically?
[09:12] Evan Cho: There are two levers: routing policy (route to cheaper model) and graceful degradation (reduce max tokens or increase temperature). We also support rate limit-based fallback to preserve budget.
[09:24] Lena Ortiz: Any examples of cost numbers we can cite to procurement?
[09:28] Evan Cho: For your traffic a rough estimate: INT8 reduces model compute cost ~35-40% vs FP16 baseline; FP8 sits around 20-25% savings but better fidelity. We'll produce a detailed cost sheet.

[09:45] (pause, typing)
[09:50] Evan Cho: I'll show the sandbox sheet now — here's per-prompt delta. You can filter by route and by prompt template. There are two templates with significant regression under INT8 (IDs in the sheet).
[10:08] Lena Ortiz: OK, we'll review and mark blockers. If those templates are critical we may pin them to FP8 permanently.

[10:20] Maya Patel: Quick note: we included competitor comparison in the deck. We try to be neutral but the main difference is that Redwood's integrated rollback and telemetry are first-class — competitors often require stitching multiple tools.
[10:33] Priya Singh: Who else do we need on follow-ups? Security and procurement will join.
[10:37] Lena Ortiz: I'll loop in David (compliance) and Sarah (procurement).

[10:45] Evan Cho: Next demo step is to provision a sandbox with 30-day telemetry and run the sensitivity sweep at low, medium, high thresholds. I'll need your prompt set and evaluation mapping.
[10:58] Marcus Hale: We'll provide prompts and list of protected attributes to redact.

[11:10] Maya Patel: Recap and next steps coming up. Any last questions?
[11:14] Lena Ortiz: No, thanks. This was helpful.
[11:18] Maya Patel: Great, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed timeline.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

NOTES/IMPERFECTIONS: occasional mis-transcriptions ("KV cash", "eff P eight"), speaker labels may shift mid-file (e.g., 'Speaker 1' appears in some segments), punctuation and sentence cuts preserved to mimic raw transcript.
